clue.text: One eye, say, kept on new baby's nightmares

indicators.note: kept on places the sounded letter on the end of the new baby piece

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a cub is a young animal, a baby

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be taken by its sound when spoken

parts.note: the word eye, spoken, gives the letter I

explanation.surface: A parent keeps a watchful eye on a newborn who is having bad dreams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you to hear 'eye' as the letter I. INCUBI are the demons once thought to cause nightmares.
explanation.definitionFit: Incubi were demons believed to lie on sleepers, and the old sense of nightmare is exactly such a smothering spirit.

clue.text: This month, one's in demand

indicators.note: in places the one-is piece inside the this-month abbreviation

parts.note: inst., short for instant, is old commercial shorthand for this month
one's reads as one is: I for one, then IS

explanation.surface: A complaint that this month one is in demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inst' (instant) is old business-letter shorthand for this month.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist is to demand firmly, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: Journalist's charge about graduates losing head

indicators.note: about means the charge word goes round the beheaded graduates

parts.note: a charge is a price, a cost

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the graduates word goes

parts.note: alumni are a college's graduates

explanation.surface: A reporter's fee for covering a story about former students.
explanation.definitionFit: A columnist is a journalist who writes a regular column; the 's reads as is, so the clue says the journalist is this.

clue.text: Aristocrat with lines in him showing up?

definitions.text: Aristocrat with lines in him showing up?

indicators.note: showing up, in a down clue, means the whole assembled piece reads from bottom to top
in places the lines abbreviation inside the aristocrat word, before the turn

parts.note: a nob is slang for an aristocrat or toff
RY, railway, is the usual crossword abbreviation for lines

explanation.surface: A nobleman whose poetry makes him conspicuous.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Byron was both a peer and a poet, so the whole clue describes him: an aristocrat with lines of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: George Gordon, Lord Byron, was a peer famous for his verse, so he is an aristocrat full of poetic lines.

clue.text: Dance craze used Coward's work

parts.note: the hay is an old country dance
a fever is a craze or frenzy of enthusiasm

explanation.surface: A dance fad took over a playwright's work.
explanation.walkthrough: Hay Fever is a 1925 comedy by Noël Coward; 'Coward' is the playwright, not a timid person.
explanation.definitionFit: Noël Coward wrote the comic play of that title, so it is one of his works.

clue.text: Something nobody's prepared to say

parts.note: reads as a taboo remark, but means a line spoken without preparation, made up on the spot

explanation.surface: A remark so awkward that no one dares utter it.
explanation.definitionFit: An improvised remark is unrehearsed: no one has prepared it before speaking.

clue.text: Stopped in Bedford after accident

indicators.note: after an accident things are mangled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Traffic in a Bedfordshire town was halted after a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is fodder, not a link: IN plus BEDFORD gives nine letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forbidden is prohibited, i.e. stopped from happening.

clue.text: Lie in tub? Not I -I ran it, perhaps

indicators.note: in places the shortened lie inside the tub word

parts.note: a vat is a large tub

indicators.note: not I asks for the letter I to be taken out of the word lie

explanation.surface: Someone declines a lazy soak, protesting that they only filled the bath.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition imagines the answer speaking: a valet might say he ran the bath for his master.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentleman's personal servant traditionally draws his employer's bath, so he could say he ran it.

clue.text: Anxious struggles — not with wife, but with son

indicators.note: not with means the wife letter is taken out of the struggles word

parts.note: wrestles means struggles

explanation.surface: A fretful couple quarrel, the husband now with his son rather than his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Being restless, unable to settle, is a sign of being anxious or uneasy.

clue.text: Almost what one hopes to hear from dowser?

definitions.text: what one hopes to hear from dowser?
definitions.meaning: a water diviner hopes to announce that a well is near

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means nearly, and split up it is a dowser's news that a well lies close by.

clue.text: Naturally, it powers a couple of rooms

parts.note: a solar is an upper private room in a medieval house
a cell is a small room, as in a monastery or prison

explanation.surface: Something that supplies the energy for a pair of rooms in a house.
explanation.walkthrough: A SOLAR was a medieval upper chamber; 'Naturally' points to sunlight, the natural source of the power.
explanation.definitionFit: A photovoltaic panel unit generates electricity from sunlight, a natural power source.

clue.text: Laws of game not so short

parts.note: RU, rugby union, is the usual crossword game

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: less means not so, as in less big

explanation.surface: The regulations of a sport are not quite so brief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laws of game' wants to be the definition; only 'Laws' is, and 'of' links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Rules are regulations, the same thing as laws.

clue.text: Change sides in discussion group to be so influential

indicators.note: change sides means the right-hand letter R is swapped for L, left

parts.note: a seminar is a small discussion group of students

explanation.surface: Switching allegiance in a debating class proves to be decisive.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminal work is highly influential, shaping later developments.

clue.text: Port is offered by British to the left

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Port wine is served by the British, passed to the left.
explanation.walkthrough: Port is traditionally passed to the left at British dinners, but here 'Port' means a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bristol, in south-west England, is a historic seaport.

clue.text: Objected to entering royal address — it's a matter of principle

indicators.note: entering means the objected word goes inside the royal address

parts.note: Your Highness is a form of address for royalty
minded means objected to, as in do you mind?

explanation.surface: Someone protested at the intrusion into a speech by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Being guided by lofty moral principles is what this quality means, so it is a matter of principle.

clue.text: As pet, she's fun if played with

indicators.note: played with means the letters are toyed with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman is amused as she fusses over her pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet' is not an animal: a pet is a sulk, as in 'in a pet'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet is a fit of sulking, and a huff is the same peevish mood.

clue.text: Eats fish, with disagreeable consequences

parts.note: downs means eats or swallows quickly
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone eats fish and suffers for it afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A downside is the drawback or unpleasant result of something.

clue.text: Free from old partner — divorce centre sent up a note

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: sent up, in a down clue, means the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Reno, Nevada, was famed as a place for quick divorces
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone is released from a former spouse after the divorce court ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divorce centre' looks like the middle letters of divorce; it is RENO, the Nevada city known for quick divorces.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to clear of blame, i.e. to set free from a charge.

clue.text: Made up ground

definitions.meaning: wearing cosmetics, face covered in make-up

explanation.definitionFit: A face wearing make-up is dusted with it, and something milled into dust has been crushed fine.

clue.text: Idle pupil's view may be summarily rejected

definitions.meaning: a daydreaming schoolchild gazes at the scene beyond the classroom glass

explanation.definitionFit: A bored pupil stares beyond the glass, and an idea discarded is figuratively thrown away through it.

clue.text: Run in the flesh?

definitions.meaning: a run of luck or wins, a series
dashing naked through a public place

explanation.definitionFit: A series of wins is a winning run, and dashing about naked in public is the other sense.

clue.text: Vagrant has to carry one set of papers

indicators.note: to carry means the vagrant word holds the one inside it

parts.note: a dosser is a tramp or rough sleeper
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A tramp has to carry a bundle of documents.
explanation.definitionFit: A dossier is a file of documents on a subject.

clue.text: Pigs said to get thorough wash

indicators.note: said means the word for pigs is heard rather than read

parts.note: sows are female pigs

explanation.surface: Pigs are said to need a good scrub.
explanation.definitionFit: A souse is a drenching or soaking in liquid, a thorough wetting.

clue.text: Use a blade and cut down tree

parts.note: to row is to work an oar, whose flat end is the blade

indicators.note: cut down means the last letter of and is chopped off

explanation.surface: Someone uses a blade to fell a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blade' suggests an axe, but it is the blade of an oar.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowan, or mountain ash, is a tree with red berries.

clue.text: One who painted less well? Exactly!

parts.note: sicker means more ill, less well
to a T means exactly

explanation.surface: An artist whose health was worse, just so.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter Sickert was a British painter of the Camden Town Group.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Sickert was an English painter, so he is one who painted.

clue.text: Keep foot away from bomb hole, in case

indicators.note: the foot of a down entry is its last letter, which is to be removed

parts.note: a crater is the hole left by a bomb

explanation.surface: Advice to keep clear of a bomb site in case of danger.
explanation.definitionFit: A crate is a wooden box or packing case.

clue.text: Direct flight to European capital

parts.note: a rout is a disorderly retreat, a flight

indicators.note: capital here means the opening, capital letter of the word

explanation.surface: A non-stop flight to a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Direct flight' reads as one idea, but 'Direct' is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To route something is to send it along a path, i.e. to direct it.

clue.text: No slouch hat?

definitions.meaning: a soft felt hat with a broad brim

explanation.definitionFit: Someone fully alert is no slouch, and a wide-brimmed felt hat bears the same name.

clue.text: Assuming clothes may be spread on the bed

definitions.text: may be spread on the bed
definitions.meaning: manure or compost laid on a garden bed, or a sauce on a bed of salad

explanation.definitionFit: Putting on clothes is getting dressed, and compost or manure put on a garden plot is a top-coat for it.

clue.text: Theologian has chapter at end of work to embellish

parts.note: the Venerable Bede was an Anglo-Saxon monk and theologian

indicators.note: at end of picks out the final letter of work

explanation.surface: A scholar adds a chapter at the end of his work to dress it up.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedeck is to decorate or adorn, the same as embellish.
